newsitem.title: USA: Wyle Electronics sees lower Q3 net.
newsitem.headline: Wyle Electronics sees lower Q3 net.

text.p: Wyle Electronics Thursday said it expects earnings for the third quarter ending September 30 to be lower than the current year's second quarter as well as the third quarter from the prior year.

Ralph Ozorkiewicz, president and chief executive officer, attributed the shortfall to "the challenging semiconductor market environment" that began in the second quarter and has continued through the first two months of the current quarter.

"Due to the soft business levels in July and August we now anticipate a sequential decline in revenues of between five and 10 percent from the second quarter," he said. "With overall gross margins trending somewhat lower from the preceding quarter, our third quarter earnings will likely decrease from the second quarter by a more significant percentage."

For the third quarter ended September 30, 1995, the company reported a profit of $10.1 million, or $0.80 per share, on sales of $273 million. In the second quarter ended June 30, 1996, net income amounted to $11.1 million, or $0.86 per share, on sales of $307 million.
"The longer term outlook for the industry, and for Wyle in particular, continues to be positive," the company said.
